text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The parliamentary opposition will propose a no confidence vote against Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi today and the vote will take place before Thursday. The Centre Party, one of the larger opposition parties, has not yet said how it will vote.
- The state court will today discuss the case against President Lennart Meri, who is alleged by two MPs to have lied during his oath of office by saying he did not help the KGB during the Soviet era.
- Russia is refusing to hand over two men alleged to have committed murder and a robbery in Estonia.
- A total 18,800 families were paid some 88.7 million kroons in welfare benefits in 1996.
- The number of unemployed graduates from secondary schools doubled in 1996 and reached 1,500.
- Meri starts a three-day visit to France on February 12.
- The government is preparing legislation which calls for duty-free zones at Tallinn ports, intended to increase their turnover.
